name: LM6171 / LM6172 (National high-speed low-distortion voltage-feedback op-amp, single/dual)
tagline: National's 100 MHz bipolar VFB video op-amp (LM6171 3600 V/us, LM6172 3000 V/us). Rollers call it neutral and detailed, but opinion is split and it is layout-sensitive.
technology: Bipolar high-speed voltage-feedback (VFB) amplifier, unity-gain stable, built for video and high-speed use. It was made on National's VIP3 complementary bipolar process: TI PCN 20241217001.1 names 'DL-LIN VIP3, 150 mm' as the LM6172's current process. The LM6171 is the single, with A and B offset grades; the LM6172 is the dual. Vendor figures: 100 MHz unity-gain bandwidth; slew rate 3600 V/us (LM6171) and 3000 V/us (LM6172); supply current 2.5 mA (LM6171) and 2.3 mA per channel (LM6172). Since the Dec 2024 PCN, the LM6172 is also built on TI's BICOMHD process at FFAB on 200 mm wafers, with a changed die.

lineage.notes: National's SPICE Op-Amp Macromodels v4.30 (18 April 1996) already has LM6171A/NS and LM6171B/NS and logs 'Models added: LM6172' on 16-APR-96. TI-imported headers give original dates of MAY 1998 (LM6171, SNOS745) and MAY 1999 (LM6172, SNOS792). Both are later than the 1996 models, so they are not first-release dates. The LM6172 was fabbed on National's VIP3 bipolar process (the PCN calls it 'DL-LIN VIP3', 150 mm wafers). Legacy URLs national.com/ds/LM/LM6171.pdf and LM6172.pdf come from the gEDA spicelib index.

Datasheets: LM6171 SNOS745 (C Mar 2013, D Nov 2023) and LM6172 SNOS792 (C Sep 2004, D Mar 2013, E Dec 2024). PCN 20241217001.1 (18 Dec 2024; proposed first ship 18 Mar 2025) adds FFAB with the BICOMHD process (FR-BIP-1, 200 mm) for the LM6172, with a changed die. It also adds a TI Mexico assembly site alongside TI Melaka. QML, QML-SP and bare-die (-MDE) LM6172 variants exist.

reputation.summary: A cult op-amp-rolling pick, not a mainstream audio part, and opinion is split. JP: nabe's Chu-Moy comparison ranked the LM6172 'straightest' (least coloured), ahead of the OP275. A Zigsow reviewer calls the LM6172IN/NOPB 'simply a high-speed stone'. Other JP listeners are negative: a goo blog post is titled 'LM6172 無駄買いですよ' (a wasted purchase), and others report light bass or say it resolves less than the LM4562 as a buffer. diyAudio posters call the LM6171/6172 'very detailed and neutral'. Head-Fi threads give mixed impressions, from neutral and clean to 'too thick/sombre' or 'technical, slightly cold'. The Chinese DiyEden/Soomal notes (2005) translate an English CMoy test; they are not independent CN opinion. They report stronger bass than the OPA132/134 and say it goes soft rather than harsh when supply-starved. Commercial use: per a Soomal teardown, the Shanling H1.1 DAC (2013) uses LM6171s in its headphone module. A CMoy noise-floor ranking that puts the LM6172 lowest is attributed, unconfirmed, to a UIUC Physics 406 student report. No ASR or Groner measurement was found. All these impressions predate the Dec 2024 LM6172 die change (PCN 20241217001.1).
sonic_descriptors: more powerful bass than OPA132/134 (DiyEden translation)
soft and round when supply-starved, not harsh (DiyEden translation)
typical_uses: Op-amp rolling in Chu-Moy/CMoy headphone amps
Headphone output stage (the Shanling H1.1 DAC uses the LM6171)
DAC I/V or output stages in DIY builds
Video and high-speed signal paths, ADC drivers (original target market)
caveats: Layout- and stability-sensitive ('cranky' per AMB forum and Head-Fi). Needs tight decoupling; risky in sockets and adapters.
Not beginner-friendly; the result depends heavily on the surrounding circuit (DiyEden translation).
Opinion is split: praise (nabe, diyAudio) sits beside negative JP reviews and mixed Head-Fi impressions.
Bass descriptions conflict between the JP reports and the translated CMoy notes.
The DiyEden/Soomal translation wrongly calls it FET-input. The LM6171/6172 is bipolar.
From 2025, LM6172 stock may carry the new BICOMHD die (PCN 20241217001.1). Listening reports refer to the older VIP3 silicon.
All praise is subjective listening; there are no vendor audio-THD claims.

part_numbers_affected: LM6172 family (the PCN says 'select devices'; specific orderables were not captured)
silicon_changes.identification: New material goes with datasheet SNOS792E (the previous revision was D). Per the PCN, TI Melaka and TI Mexico assembly differ in lead finish (matte Sn vs NiPdAu), mount and mold compound, and pin-1 designator (notch vs dimple). The site-to-feature mapping should be read from the PCN. These features show only the assembly site, not the fab. Because FFAB is added rather than replacing DL-LIN, old (VIP3) and new (BICOMHD) die can ship under the same orderable. Parts with date codes from 2025 onward are the ones at risk. Whether the LM6171 single is covered by this PCN was not confirmed.
silicon_changes.summary: TI qualified FFAB (Freising) with the BICOMHD process (FR-BIP-1, 200 mm) for the LM6172, alongside the original National DL-LIN VIP3 process (150 mm). The die changed as a result. This is part of TI's exit from 150 mm fabs. The same part number now covers two different silicon builds on different bipolar processes.

spec_deltas.after: TI Melaka or TI Mexico (added), with different lead finish, mold/mount compound and pin-1 mark

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Unknown. A new bipolar process and die can change noise, distortion, slew and phase margin. All LM6172 listening impressions predate 2025 and refer to VIP3 silicon. Rollers should not assume new stock sounds or behaves the same, especially in the layout-sensitive, socketed builds this part is known for.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium: the die was redesigned on a different bipolar process, and the SNOS792E electrical changes were not captured. Stability margins in high-speed, socketed circuits could differ.
silicon_changes.verification: This entry was not from the sweep and was kept as adversarially checked by an earlier pass. Two extra WebSearches did not surface the PCN 20241217001 text or show whether LM6171 is included. Search snippets of the current LM6172 datasheet still describe the part as VIP III, so check the SNOS792E revision history for the BICOMHD note.

silicon_changes.when: PDN 20230906005 (rev .3), 2023. The LM6171 datasheet was revised to SNOS745D in November 2023.
part_numbers_affected: LM6171BIN (listed obsolete by distributors; not confirmed in the PDN text)
silicon_changes.identification: Discontinuance of the B-grade LM6171 orderables, not a silicon change. The A grade (LM6171AIM/NOPB, LM6171AIMX/NOPB) remains Active, and the PDN names LM6171AIMX/NOPB as the pin-to-pin replacement. Any B-grade part sold now is old stock.
silicon_changes.summary: TI PDN 20230906005.3, 'Discontinuance of Select Devices', includes LM6171BIM, with LM6171AIMX/NOPB recommended as the pin-to-pin replacement. DigiKey lists LM6171BIM/NOPB as obsolete and no longer manufactured. The LM6171 family itself remains Active in the A grade. The Nov 2023 datasheet revision (SNOS745D) coincides with the PDN. Its change notes were not seen, so no spec delta is claimed.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: None to the silicon. The B and A grades are selections of the same die. Only B-grade availability is affected.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: grade discontinuance only. The recommended A-grade replacement has the same pinout and is the higher-grade selection.
silicon_changes.verification: New in this curation pass. Two WebSearches found PDN 20230906005.3 listing LM6171BIM with LM6171AIMX/NOPB as the replacement, and DigiKey showing LM6171BIM/NOPB obsolete. This comes from search summaries only; the PDN PDF was not read, and LM6171BIN's presence in it is unconfirmed.

counterfeit_notes: No specific counterfeit or remarking reports for the LM6171 or LM6172 were found. The DIP-8 LM6172IN and LM6171BIN are the parts rollers want. Marketplace DIP listings exist (e.g. Amazon.co.jp 'Phoncoo' LM6172IN DIP8). Genuine TI-era LM6172IN/NOPB DIP has been retailed by Bispa and eleshop.jp. Check the logo (National vs TI), date code, laser marking and /NOPB labelling. Separately, since PCN 20241217001.1 (first ship Mar 2025), genuine LM6172 can carry a new BICOMHD die. A 2025+ date code, NiPdAu leads or a different pin-1 mark do not mean a fake; they may be new-process parts.

open_questions: What changed in the SNOS792E electrical tables (slew, noise, Vos, THD, stability) with the BICOMHD die? The revision-history section was not captured.
Which LM6172 orderables does PCN 20241217001.1 cover (SOIC only, or also the PDIP LM6172IN/NOPB and QML variants)? Does TI keep shipping VIP3 die in parallel?
Why was LM6171 SNOS745D (Nov 2023) issued? Is there a matching LM6171 fab/process PCN? None was found.
SNOS792C's indexed header reads 'MAY 2004 – REVISED SEPTEMBER 2004', while rev D/E say 'MAY 1999'. Check against the PDF.

National DS document numbers and revision chain for the LM6171 and LM6172 are unknown; recover them from Wayback captures of the national.com URLs. The TI header original dates (May 1998 for LM6171, May 1999 for LM6172) are later than the April 1996 macromodels.

The DIP-scarcity hint (discovery) was neither confirmed nor refuted by web search. TI-era LM6172IN/NOPB DIP has been retailed in Japan. Lifecycle (active/NRND/obsolete) of all orderables, including the LM6171 DIP, is still unverified.
Does the LM6171 still ship in both A and B grades (LM6171AIM/NOPB and LM6171BIM/NOPB copies exist)?

refuted_claims: 'No second source, die change or PCN was found' (draft lineage and open questions) is refuted. TI PCN 20241217001.1 (18 Dec 2024) adds FFAB BICOMHD 200 mm silicon with a changed die for the LM6172, and the datasheet moves SNOS792D to SNOS792E.
The draft's empty silicon_changes list is refuted; the PCN above is a same-part-number, different-silicon hazard.
'LM6171 TI literature number not found; do not use SNOS745' is refuted: the LM6171 datasheet is SNOS745 (SNOS745C Mar 2013, SNOS745D Nov 2023).

The old-style title 'LM6171 High Speed Low Power Low Distortion Voltage Feedback Amplifier' for the current LM6171 symlink is refuted. The current title is 'LM6171 High-Speed, Low-Power, Low-Distortion Voltage Feedback Amplifier'; the old title belongs to SNOS745C and earlier.
The current LM6172 revision is not an unknown letter after D: it is SNOS792E, revised December 2024.

Counterfeit notes: a 2025+ date code, NiPdAu leads or a different pin-1 mark may indicate new-process genuine parts, not fakes.
claims_confirmed: The LM6171 datasheet is SNOS745C, 'MAY 1998 – REVISED MARCH 2013' (https://datasheet.octopart.com/LM6171BIM-NOPB-Texas-Instruments-datasheet-102490848.pdf; https://www.mouser.com/datasheet/2/282/lm6171-45603.pdf)
The current LM6171 datasheet is SNOS745D, revised November 2023, titled 'LM6171 High-Speed, Low-Power, Low-Distortion Voltage Feedback Amplifier' (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lm6171.pdf)
The current LM6172 datasheet is SNOS792E, 'MAY 1999 – REVISED DECEMBER 2024' (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lm6172.pdf)
SNOS792D 'MAY 1999 – REVISED MARCH 2013' survives on the PUC-Rio mirror (https://www.maxwell.vrac.puc-rio.br/21708/21708_4.PDF)
SNOS792C 'MAY 2004 – REVISED SEPTEMBER 2004' survives on Octopart under LM6172IN (https://datasheet.octopart.com/LM6172IN-Texas-Instruments-datasheet-12525018.pdf)

PCN 20241217001.1 was issued 18 Dec 2024, with proposed first ship 18 Mar 2025. It adds FFAB with the BICOMHD process (FR-BIP-1, 200 mm) in addition to DL-LIN VIP3 (150 mm), with a changed die, and adds TI Mexico assembly (lead finish, compounds and pin-1 mark differ). The LM6172 datasheet moves from SNOS792D to SNOS792E (https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/6025/PCN20241217001.1.pdf)
LM6171: 3600 V/us slew, 100 MHz unity-gain bandwidth, 2.5 mA supply current (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lm6171.pdf, via search summary)

The TI product pages LM6171, LM6172, LM6172QML, LM6172QML-SP and the LM6172IM/NOPB part-details page exist (https://www.ti.com/product/LM6172QML-SP; https://www.ti.com/product/LM6172/part-details/LM6172IM/NOPB)
The Carnegie Observatories mirror holds an old-style-title LM6172 datasheet (https://instrumentation.obs.carnegiescience.edu/ccd/parts/LM6172.pdf)

revision_chain_notes: LM6171 (single). National DS012336 is newly identified from the datasheetcatalog filename. Known chain: National DS012336 edition(s), undated in the search results; the TI header gives an original date of May 1998; the 1996 SPICE models suggest an earlier first release. Then TI SNOS745B, implied and unconfirmed. Then SNOS745C (March 2013, header seen; new copy at danomsk.ru). Then SNOS745D (November 2023). Missing: National DS012336 edition dates and revisions, and SNOS745 A/B dates. Several National-era copies were found with revision not shown: pdf.datasheetcatalog DS012336.PDF, DigiKey media, Octopart LM6171BIN, alldatasheet 9003/NSC, ChipFind, datasheet4u, manualmachine, PE2BZ, waynestegall, yumpu. LM6172 (dual). The National DS number is still not found in these searches. Known chain: National edition(s) (TI gives an original date of May 1999; the LM6172 SPICE model was added on 16 April 1996). Alldatasheet has two distinct National uploads: a 16-page, 551 KB early edition (IDs 9004/9005/9008) and a 25-page, 1 MB NOPB-era edition (ID 578684), dates not shown. Then SNOS792C, which is odd: its indexed header reads 'MAY 2004 – REVISED SEPTEMBER 2004'. Then SNOS792D (March 2013) and SNOS792E (December 2024, BICOMHD die change per PCN 20241217001.1). Missing: the National DS number, National edition dates, SNOS792A/B, and change lists for all TI revisions. No second sources were found.
